name: Cash
oneLiner: Notes and coins. Instant to spend, but The Melt shrinks it every year.
realLife: Cash earns nothing. With inflation around 4–6% a year in India, its buying power falls every year you hold it.

name: Savings Account
oneLiner: A bank account that pays a little interest, usually less than inflation.
realLife: Most banks pay roughly 2.5–4% a year. Deposits are insured by DICGC up to ₹5 lakh per depositor per bank. Minors can open one with a parent or guardian.

name: Fixed Deposit
oneLiner: Lock money with a bank for a fixed time at a fixed rate.
realLife: Bank FDs lock a rate for 7 days to 10 years. Breaking one early usually costs a small penalty. Insured by DICGC up to ₹5 lakh per depositor per bank. Interest is taxable.

name: Recurring Deposit
oneLiner: A monthly FD: put in a fixed amount every month for a fixed time.
realLife: Banks and post offices offer RDs from ₹100 a month. It builds the SIP habit with FD-like safety and FD-like returns.

name: Public Provident Fund
oneLiner: A government-backed savings scheme with a 15-year lock-in and tax-free interest.
realLife: The government sets the PPF rate every quarter. You can invest ₹500 to ₹1.5 lakh a year, and partial withdrawals open from year 7. A parent can open one for a minor.

name: Index Fund
oneLiner: Buy a whole basket of companies in one go, at a very low cost.
realLife: A Nifty 50 index fund owns India's 50 largest listed companies in the same proportions as the index. Costs (expense ratios) are often well under 0.5% a year. Prices swing in the short term.

name: SIP
traits: Invest a fixed amount every month
Buys more units when prices are low
Builds discipline: no timing needed
oneLiner: Systematic Investment Plan: invest a fixed amount on a fixed date, automatically.
realLife: Most mutual funds in India accept SIPs from about ₹100–₹500 a month. Consistency matters more than the amount.
watchOut: Stopping and restarting breaks the snowball

name: Lump Sum
traits: Invest all at once
Wins in steadily rising markets
Feels painful if prices fall right after
oneLiner: Invest a big amount in one go, like a gift or bonus.
realLife: When you get a big amount (e.g. birthday money), you can invest it at once or spread it as a SIP over a few months. Both beat leaving it idle.

name: Government Bond
oneLiner: Lend money to the government. It pays you fixed interest and returns your money later.
realLife: Individuals can buy government securities through RBI Retail Direct. Prices move when interest rates change.

name: Mutual Fund
oneLiner: Many investors pool money, and a professional manager invests it for them.
realLife: Each unit has a NAV (price). Funds charge an expense ratio every year. ELSS funds have a 3-year lock-in.
watchOut: Picking funds on past returns alone

name: Gold
oneLiner: A commodity that often holds value when inflation or fear spikes.
realLife: Besides jewellery, Indians can own gold through gold ETFs, gold mutual funds, and government Sovereign Gold Bonds when they are on offer.

name: Stocks
oneLiner: Own a slice of one company. Share its growth and its troubles.
realLife: Shares trade on the NSE and BSE through a demat account. Minors can hold a demat account operated by a guardian. Single companies can fall a long way.

name: REIT
oneLiner: Own a small slice of rent-paying office buildings and malls.
realLife: Real Estate Investment Trusts are listed on Indian exchanges and must pay out most of their income to unit holders.

name: Futures & Options
oneLiner: Contracts whose value depends on another asset. Great for hedging, dangerous for gambling.
realLife: A SEBI study found about 9 in 10 individual F&O traders lost money over FY22–FY24. Professionals mostly use options to hedge risk, like insurance.

name: Crypto
oneLiner: Digital tokens like bitcoin. Prices swing wildly and differ across exchanges.
realLife: In India, gains on crypto (virtual digital assets) are taxed at 30% with 1% TDS on transfers. Exchanges are not regulated like stock exchanges. Studied here as a case of speculation and arbitrage.

name: Private Equity & VC
oneLiner: Back private companies and startups before they list. Most fail; a few win big.
realLife: In India, most people access PE and VC through Alternative Investment Funds, which usually need at least ₹1 crore and lock money for years.

name: Emergency Fund
oneLiner: Money kept ready for surprises, so you never have to sell investments in a hurry.
realLife: A common rule of thumb is 3–6 months of expenses, kept in a savings account or a liquid fund you can get the same day. For a teen it can be much smaller: enough for a broken phone or a lost bus pass.
watchOut: Too much in cash melts with inflation
traits: Kept somewhere instant
Used only for real surprises
Refilled after you use it

name: ELSS Fund
oneLiner: A share-market mutual fund that saves tax, with a 3-year lock-in.
realLife: ELSS (Equity Linked Savings Scheme) funds invest mostly in shares. Under the old tax regime, up to ₹1.5 lakh a year counts for a Section 80C deduction. Each investment is locked for 3 years, the shortest lock among 80C options.

name: Asset Allocation
traits: Split money across shares, bonds, gold and cash
More time to the goal, more room for shares
Decides most of how bumpy the ride is
oneLiner: Choose how much goes into each kind of asset, to fit your goal.
realLife: Multi-asset and balanced advantage funds in India manage a mix for you. A simple DIY version is an index fund plus a debt fund in your chosen split.

name: Hedge
traits: Pay a small cost to limit a big loss
Insurance for investments
Lowers risk; doesn't add return
oneLiner: A position that gains when your main holding loses.
realLife: Farmers lock crop prices with futures, airlines hedge fuel, and investors buy put options as crash insurance. In India these trade on the NSE, BSE and NCDEX.

name: Buy and Hold
traits: Buy broad, good-quality investments
Hold for years through ups and downs
Few trades, low costs, lower tax
oneLiner: Buy a diversified investment and keep it for the long run.
realLife: In India, shares held over a year pay a lower long-term capital gains tax, and every trade you skip saves brokerage and STT.

name: Fundamental Analysis
traits: Study the business, not just the price
Compare price with profit (P/E)
Check debt, ROE and growth together
oneLiner: Judge a company by its profits, debt and growth before trusting its price.
realLife: Listed companies publish quarterly results and annual reports, free on the NSE and BSE websites.
watchOut: Great companies can still be overpriced

name: Insurance
traits: Turns a disaster into a small yearly cost
Cheapest when you're young and healthy
Keep it separate from investing
oneLiner: Term life and health insurance protect your family and your plan from one bad event.
realLife: Insurance in India is regulated by IRDAI. Term life pays your family if you die during the term; health insurance pays hospital bills.
watchOut: Plans that mix insurance and investing often do both badly

name: National Pension System
oneLiner: A low-cost pension scheme: invest while you work, draw a pension after 60.
realLife: NPS is regulated by PFRDA. You choose a mix of shares, corporate bonds and government bonds. Most of it stays locked until 60, and part must buy a pension (an annuity).
